section_summary: This section records inquiries about Japanese bonds, blocked assets and dollar–yen stabilization, alongside reports on Japanese gold shipments and banking activity in Latin America. A Tokyo financial report includes budget and debt analysis, statistical tables, translated ordinances and an account of the difficulties Americans faced when leaving Japan. The section ends with the beginning of a 1942 speech by Finance Minister Okinobu Kaya on wartime finance and the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere.

subfiles.title: Request for reports on dollar–yen stabilization
subfiles.about: The Federal Reserve Bank of New York asks for any further reports on a dollar–yen stabilization proposal.
subfiles.summary: Burnett requests material beyond the Department of State Bulletin.

subfiles.title: Reply on dollar–yen stabilization reports
subfiles.about: The Department says it has issued no additional reports on the stabilization plan.
subfiles.summary: Livesey directs Burnett to the published Department of State Bulletin.

subfiles.title: Treasury advice on Japanese letter of credit in Peru
subfiles.about: Treasury suggests a response to the Lima embassy about a Japanese bank credit and shipment.
subfiles.summary: Treasury recommends thanking Banco Italiano and requesting any further shipment information.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Lima on Japanese financial operations
subfiles.about: The embassy is asked to thank Banco Italiano and report any confirmation of a shipment.
subfiles.summary: The expired credit appears to leave no effective action concerning the shipment.

subfiles.title: Japanese gold shipments to South America
subfiles.about: Reports trace Japanese gold shipments to Peru, Argentina and Brazil.
subfiles.summary: Gold delivered in Buenos Aires was reportedly to finance Japanese purchases of Argentine goods.

subfiles.title: Official Japanese broadcasts to North America
subfiles.about: A broadcast digest covers Japanese bond sales, wartime preparations and seized funds in Tianjin.
subfiles.summary: Short items also cover Thailand, Manchukuo, the Axis pact and Japanese air defense.

subfiles.title: Economic pressure in Japan
subfiles.about: The note points to a memorandum on evidence of economic pressure in Japan.
subfiles.summary: References a December 6 memorandum filed elsewhere.

subfiles.title: Request concerning Japanese utility bonds
subfiles.about: A bondholder asks for payment of bonds issued by utility companies operating in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cullen describes the bonds as savings for old age and asks the government to pay their face value upon surrender.

subfiles.title: Reply to Nellie Cullen on utility bonds
subfiles.about: The Department responds to Cullen's request for government payment of her bonds.
subfiles.summary: Hiss knows of no legislation authorizing State or Treasury to purchase them.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about Elizabeth J. McCloy's Japanese bonds
subfiles.about: Attorneys ask how their client should handle unpaid coupons on Japanese government bonds.
subfiles.summary: McCloy holds thirty-one 1910 Japanese bonds; her November 1941 coupons went unpaid.

subfiles.title: Reply on filing a claim for McCloy's bonds
subfiles.about: The Department addresses the possibility of filing a claim over McCloy's bonds.
subfiles.summary: No government procedure for a formal claim has yet been established.

subfiles.title: Japanese collections through American banks in Havana
subfiles.about: The embassy reports a change in routing of Japanese collection proceeds after U.S. freezing measures.
subfiles.summary: A National City Bank manager says proceeds formerly sent to the Yokohama Specie Bank in New York were redirected to Banco Nacional de México.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment concerning McCloy's Japanese bonds
subfiles.about: McCloy's attorneys acknowledge the Department's response.
subfiles.summary: They note that no claims procedure exists yet.

subfiles.title: Protection of holders of Tokyo and Yokohama dollar bonds
subfiles.about: The Department discusses coupon payments and protection of U.S. holders of Japanese municipal dollar bonds.
subfiles.summary: Treasury is considering licenses for coupons that matured before December 7, 1941. Berle raises questions about whether servicing funds held by Yokohama Specie Bank are trust funds and refers White to Chester M. Carré concerning bondholders' claims.

subfiles.title: Note on Francis White's representation of bondholders
subfiles.about: Treasury is notified that White represents U.S. holders of Japanese dollar bonds.
subfiles.summary: Records State Department approval of White's representative role.

subfiles.title: Francis White's acknowledgment on Japanese dollar bonds
subfiles.about: White thanks the Department for its work on coupon payments and bondholders' claims.
subfiles.summary: White says he will contact Treasury official Carré.

subfiles.title: Payments from Yokohama Specie Bank in Rio de Janeiro
subfiles.about: Bank records reportedly show payments to eight Japanese individuals, including military attachés.
subfiles.summary: The payments occurred in Rio de Janeiro from late September to early November 1941.

subfiles.title: Review of Tokyo commercial attaché financial report
subfiles.about: A State Department review summarizes the Tokyo commercial attaché's November 1941 financial report.
subfiles.summary: It highlights Kaya's optimistic Diet address, growing war expenditure and debt, tax increases, and uncertainty about bond absorption. It cautions that available figures do not reliably measure Japan's future war capacity.

subfiles.title: Tokyo despatch transmitting special financial report
subfiles.about: The embassy transmits Special Financial Report No. 59 for November 3–17, 1941.
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch for the commercial attaché's report.

subfiles.title: Special Financial Report No. 59
subfiles.about: The report assesses Japanese wartime finance and lists sixteen enclosures.
subfiles.summary: It reviews Finance Minister Kaya's optimistic account of budgets, investment and savings while identifying pressure from freezing orders and shortages of vital materials. It describes new luxury taxes, payment of some employee bonuses in bonds, slower postal savings growth, rising demand on the Deposits Bureau and increasing uncertainty about absorption of national bonds. The final pages introduce an account of Americans' departure difficulties and list statistical and legal enclosures.

subfiles.title: Procedure for leaving Japan for America
subfiles.about: An American citizen describes permits and other steps required to leave Japan.
subfiles.summary: The account covers tax clearance, police forms, funds and baggage permits, inoculations, tickets and customs inspection. It describes the disruption caused by cancelled sailings and the alternative route through Nagasaki and Shanghai.

subfiles.title: National debt at the end of September 1941
subfiles.about: A table lists domestic and foreign Japanese debt by bond type.
subfiles.summary: It gives a grand total of about 34.05 billion yen.

subfiles.title: National Treasury statement for fiscal 1941–42
subfiles.about: A table compares Japanese ordinary and extraordinary revenue through September 1941 with September 1940.
subfiles.summary: Entries include taxes, public loans and transfers from prior surpluses.

subfiles.title: Bank deposits, loans and security holdings
subfiles.about: A table compares Japanese banking balances at the end of September 1941.
subfiles.summary: It covers deposits, loans, securities and cash.

subfiles.title: Wholesale price index, October 1941
subfiles.about: A Tokyo wholesale price table compares commodity groups with earlier months.
subfiles.summary: The total average index is reported as 202.0.

subfiles.title: Retail price index, October 1941
subfiles.about: A retail price table compares food, clothing and other goods with earlier periods.
subfiles.summary: The total average index is reported as 169.2.

subfiles.title: National debt at the end of October 1941
subfiles.about: A table updates Japanese domestic and foreign debt by bond type.
subfiles.summary: It gives a grand total of about 34.97 billion yen.

subfiles.title: Ito-Chu Shoji changes its name to Sanko Company
subfiles.about: A business report describes the merger that created Sanko Company.
subfiles.summary: It identifies the absorbed firms, new capital and Osaka headquarters, and compares recent profits and dividends.

subfiles.title: Finance Ministry Ordinance No. 62
subfiles.about: The ordinance designates foreign goods subject to import duty under the Bonded Factory Law.
subfiles.summary: It lists categories from food and fabrics to metal goods, bicycle parts and batteries.

subfiles.title: Temporary Mail Control Ordinance
subfiles.about: The ordinance authorizes wartime restrictions, inspection and withholding of mail.
subfiles.summary: It sets penalties and defines how the powers apply in several Japanese governed territories.

subfiles.title: Communications Ministry Ordinance No. 91
subfiles.about: The ordinance specifies sender identification and handling of foreign mail.
subfiles.summary: Postal officials may demand translations or proof of identity.

subfiles.title: Bonds and debentures issued during October 1941
subfiles.about: Tables list October and January–October bond and debenture issuance.
subfiles.summary: Categories include national, municipal, bank and corporate issues.

subfiles.title: Communications Ministry Ordinance No. 92
subfiles.about: The ordinance limits messages on international postal money orders and savings transfer forms.
subfiles.summary: Postal officials may remove or withhold messages considered unclear or harmful to national defense.

subfiles.title: Revision of bank capital employment regulations
subfiles.from: Okinobu Kaya; Hiroya Ino; Nobusuke Kishi; Shigenori Togo
subfiles.about: A joint ministerial ordinance adds designated capital funds to exemptions from lending controls.
subfiles.summary: The text includes the amendment and the relevant existing Article 8 provisions.

subfiles.title: Designation of capital funds under Article 8
subfiles.from: Okinobu Kaya; Hiroya Ino; Nobusuke Kishi; Shigenori Togo
subfiles.about: The notice designates munitions bill discounts and certain export loss compensation finance.
subfiles.summary: It implements the new capital fund exemption.

subfiles.title: Communications Ministry Ordinance No. 90
subfiles.about: The ordinance bars specified secret communication methods in foreign mail.
subfiles.summary: Prohibited forms include codes, invisible ink and double envelopes.

subfiles.title: Interest payments due on Japanese dollar bonds
subfiles.about: The note points to a tabulation of upcoming Japanese dollar bond interest.
subfiles.summary: It notes that many private Japanese issues had been repatriated.

subfiles.title: Interest on Japanese bonds from U.S. funds
subfiles.about: The note points to a letter asking whether Japanese bond interest may be paid from funds in the United States.
subfiles.summary: Haas asks about payment to holders regardless of wartime allegiance.

subfiles.title: Referral of Churchill bond inquiry
subfiles.about: The Department forwards an attorney's inquiry about payment on Japanese bonds from blocked assets.
subfiles.summary: It encloses Churchill's letter and the Department's reply.

subfiles.title: Reply to Churchill on Japanese bond claims
subfiles.about: The Department responds to a request for principal and interest from blocked Japanese assets.
subfiles.summary: No offset procedure is known; the inquiry is referred to the Alien Property Custodian.

subfiles.title: Churchill inquiry about Empire of Japan bonds
subfiles.about: An attorney asks whether frozen Japanese government funds can pay bondholders.
subfiles.summary: He argues that payment would let holders buy U.S. bonds.

subfiles.title: File on Tutomo Nisiyama transaction
subfiles.about: Poole forwards a file concerning the former Japanese Financial Commissioner.
subfiles.summary: The file concerns Tutomo Nisiyama's New York office property.

subfiles.title: Forwarding Nisiyama letter and furniture affidavit
subfiles.about: Poole forwards Nisiyama's letter and authorization concerning furniture at his former office.
subfiles.summary: The affidavit authorizes a sale by New York banking authorities.

subfiles.title: Forwarding New York Banking Department correspondence
subfiles.about: An immigration officer sends banking department correspondence about Nisiyama.
subfiles.summary: Lincourt asks Poole to take appropriate action.

subfiles.title: Request to deliver letter to Nisiyama
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, Immigration and Naturalization Service
subfiles.about: The Banking Department asks that its attached letter be delivered to Nisiyama.
subfiles.summary: It concerns the Japanese Financial Commission.

subfiles.title: Proposed sale of Japanese Financial Commission furniture
subfiles.about: New York's bank liquidator seeks permission to sell stored commission furniture.
subfiles.summary: Moving and continuing storage costs threaten to exceed its value.

subfiles.title: Finance Minister Kaya's speech to the Japanese Diet
subfiles.doc_type: memorandum for the files; broadcast transcript
subfiles.about: A memorandum reproduces the beginning of Kaya's May 27 speech on Japan's wartime budget and financial policy.
subfiles.summary: Kaya presents supplementary shipbuilding expenditure and portrays Japanese wartime finances as secure. He describes a Japan centered financial system for the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere, including exchange arrangements with Thailand and currency policy in occupied areas. He stresses national savings, directed lending and wartime finance banks, then compares Japan's position with U.S. wartime economic measures. The transcript continues beyond page 160.
